source.publication: 2025 Form 80-100 Resident, Non-Resident and Part-Year Resident Individual Income Tax Instructions (Rev. 12/25) and the 2025 Form 80-105 Resident Return (Rev. 09/25); Miss. Admin. Code Title 35 Part III Income and Franchise (Department of Revenue income tax regulations)
source.section: Form 80-105 page 1 lines 8-17 and page 2 lines 38-66; Instructions PDF p.5 Filing Status and Exemptions table; p.6 Additional Exemptions, Lines 8-12; p.7 Lines 14-17; p.22 Tax Rates; p.27 Schedule of Tax Computation lines 1-4; Instructions PDF p.11 Line 46 Total Pensions and Annuities; FAQ 'Is retirement income taxable?'; Miss. Admin. Code Title 35 Part III Subpart 02 Chapter 07 rules 100, 101, 103 and 104 (https://www.sos.ms.gov/adminsearch/ACCode/00000158c.pdf, PDF p.18)

worked: Federal AGI = Roth conversion (person 0) 50,000.00 = 50,000.00. Federal taxable income = 50,000.00 - 15,750.00 federal standard deduction = 34,250.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). Form 80-105 filing status box 5, Single. Start at federal AGI 50,000.00 (Mississippi builds its own income on lines 38 to 66; the projection starts from federal AGI and takes out the exempt income, the same result here). Less retirement income 50,000.00 (exempt in total, as the projection reads regulation rule 101: the taxable amount of a conversion is income from the traditional IRA, and rule 100 exempts it; rule 103 governs payouts from a Roth IRA, not conversions into one; no Mississippi source names conversions). Line 66 and line 13 Mississippi AGI = 0.00. Line 14 standard deduction 2,300.00. Line 8 age boxes checked 0; line 10 = 0 x 1,500.00 = 0.00; line 11 6,000.00; line 12 and line 15 = 6,000.00. Line 16 Mississippi taxable income = 0.00 - 2,300.00 - 6,000.00 = -8,300.00 on the formula; floored at 0.00 (the form enters 0). Schedule of Tax Computation lines 1 to 4 and line 17 = 0.00. Lines 18 and 19 credits 0.00; line 20 = 0.00. If the Department treated the conversion as not a retirement allowance, Mississippi taxable income would be 50,000.00 - 2,300.00 - 6,000.00 = 41,700.00 and tax 4.4% x 31,700.00 = 1,394.80 (the figure this case had before the 2026-11-07 decision).
accepted_approximations: Mississippi builds its own income (Form 80-105 lines 38 to 66); the projection starts from federal AGI and removes the exempt income through the reliefs and Social Security treatment.

Roth conversions are exempted on the regulation's rule 101, 'all income from ... Individual Retirement Accounts': the taxable amount of a conversion is income from the traditional IRA. No Mississippi source names conversions. If the Department treats a conversion as not a retirement allowance, this understates tax in a conversion year.
